OVERVIEW

One system. One applied case study. A visible decision trail.

The Orchestrator is the reusable method. Upgrade With Confidence is the project that shows how the method behaves when evidence is incomplete and human judgment still matters.

THE CUSTOMER QUESTION

“Before I place this order, what exactly changes?”

The case study explores how today’s payment, the next bill, recurring costs, credits and conditions could be explained before commitment.

WHY THIS EXISTS

AI can make UX work faster.
It can also make the reasoning disappear.

The Orchestrator is designed to prevent that. It makes every handoff inspectable: what entered the phase, what the AI was allowed to do, what it produced, and where a human made the call.

01

Start from something approved

No phase begins from an invisible prompt or an unmarked assumption.

02

Give AI a bounded job

Each agent has a defined responsibility, method and stopping point.

03

Make the decision human

The system can recommend a direction. Only the accountable designer can advance it.

02 · THE SYSTEM MEETS A REAL DESIGN QUESTION

A framework only matters if it can carry a messy decision from ambiguity to action.

Upgrade With Confidence

THE MOMENT WE CHOSE

“Before I place this order, what exactly changes?”

A device upgrade is not one price. It can combine tax, a device payment, a one-time fee, a plan effect and a trade-in credit that may arrive later. Our design hypothesis is simple: bring those consequences together before commitment.

TodayWhat leaves my account now?Next billWhich new charges appear once?Every monthWhat changes after credits begin?ConditionsWhat could still change the amount?

THE EXPERT METHOD

Ten heuristics turned visual observations into testable design risks.

This is expert evaluation—not customer evidence. Severity describes potential risk, not how often customers experience it.

H1 · SEVERITY 3Visibility of system status

The complete financial state is not consolidated before commitment.

H3 · SEVERITY 4User control and freedom

The connected path does not show a complete editable pre-submit review.

H5 · SEVERITY 3Error prevention

Financial confirmation and ambiguous-order recovery are not demonstrated.

H6 · SEVERITY 4Recognition over recall

Payment, plan, offer and trade-in values must be remembered across sections.

03 · THE DESIGN RESPONSE

Preserve the journey. Add the missing financial layer.

The familiar line, device-grid, PDP, plan, payment, trade-in, review and confirmation patterns remain. Upgrade Impact sits alongside them, explains the math and stays editable until commitment.

Familiar flow retainedTotals and deltas togetherEdit without losing contextRecover without duplicating

05 · THE NEXT EVIDENCE GAP

Workflow validation tells us that it works. Customer testing must tell us whether it is understood.

No participant preference is claimed. The next credible step is a comparative comprehension study using the same upgrade scenario in the current and proposed experiences.

COMPLETED

Expert and workflow evaluation

Heuristic review, deterministic paths, keyboard behavior, responsive reflow and targeted recovery retest.

NEXT STUDY

Current versus proposed

Can representative participants correctly explain today’s payment, next bill, ongoing bill and trade-in conditions?

MEASURES

Evidence before preference

Comprehension accuracy, critical errors, completion, time, backtracking, confidence and reasoned preference.

Required wording: “The proposed design is ready for participant testing.” Not: “Customers preferred the proposed design.”

06 · WHEN THE FLOW IS NOT THE ANSWER

The transaction handles choices. Upgrade Guide handles questions.

Upgrade Guide is a separate public-information proof of concept—not part of the synthetic Northstar transaction. It explains general Verizon upgrade topics without pretending it can see a customer’s account.

Useful for public guidance

Eligibility rules, phone selection, trade-in conditions, plans, activation and support.

Stops at the account boundary

No account access, order inspection, bill lookup, live inventory or guaranteed offer.

Grounded in a verified 150-question public FAQ set. When the answer depends on private account data, it escalates instead of guessing.

ELIGIBILITYTRADE-INACTIVATION
PUBLIC GUIDANCE

Questions do not have to interrupt the story.

Upgrade Guide now sits above the case study. Open it from any chapter, ask a general upgrades question, then return to the same place.

No account access · No live offer lookup · No guessing

ASK THE GUIDE

General upgrade information, with a visible stopping point.

Ask about eligibility, phones, plans, trade-ins, activation or support. The assistant will not pretend it can inspect a private account, order or bill.

07 · WHERE THE STORY MUST STOP

A credible case study says where its evidence ends.

This submission demonstrates a governed process and an executable design hypothesis. It does not turn a synthetic exercise into a customer or business claim.

SUPPORTED
  • Six-phase orchestration
  • Artifact and decision traceability
  • Executable prototype behavior
  • Revision and targeted retest
  • Grounded FAQ response boundaries
NOT YET SUPPORTED
  • Real customer usability
  • Measured conversion lift
  • Production feasibility
  • Accessibility conformance
  • Live account or order integration

THE PRODUCT-OWNER CASE

How we would prove whether the redesign works.

This section translates the UX idea into a business decision: what should improve, how we would measure it and what must not get worse.

WHY THIS SECTION EXISTS

A better-looking experience is not enough to justify investment.

The Product Owner Case shows how we would evaluate this redesign as a business investment—not claim that it has already increased conversion or retention.

  1. 01

    What customer behavior should improve?Customers should understand the financial impact with less hesitation and reconstruction.

  2. 02

    Which business outcome should we measure?Review-to-submit conversion in a controlled product experiment.

  3. 03

    What consequences must we protect against?Cancellations, returns, billing contacts and promotion disputes must not worsen.

01 · CONFIRM COMPREHENSIONCan people explain the math?

Check today’s payment, next bill, ongoing bill and credit timing with participants.

→
02 · OBSERVE BEHAVIORDoes hesitation decrease?

Watch review exits, backtracks and jumps to support during the task.

→
03 · MEASURE THE OUTCOMEDoes completion improve?

Run a controlled experiment on review-to-submit conversion.

→
04 · PROTECT QUALITYDid we create new problems?

Monitor cancellations, returns, billing contacts and promotion disputes.

The decision sequence: customer study first → controlled product experiment second → rollout only if conversion improves and quality guardrails hold.

NEXT EVIDENCE STEPComparative Comprehension Study
PROPOSED CUSTOMER TEST · NOT COMPLETED YET

Can people explain the bill more accurately in the new design?

Participants complete the same upgrade in both versions. We compare what they understood—not only which screen they liked.

THE QUESTION

Can participants correctly explain what they pay—and when?

  • Amount due today
  • Estimated next bill and the one-time fee
  • Ongoing monthly bill after credits
  • Trade-in amount, timing and conditions
THE METHOD

Moderated, within-subject comparison

  • 8–12 representative upgrade customers
  • Order counterbalanced to reduce learning bias
  • Same device, plan and trade-in scenario
  • Think-aloud task plus comprehension questions
01Comprehension accuracy

Correctly state all four financial outcomes without prompting.

02Critical errors

Track wrong amounts, missed fees and mistaken credit timing.

03Behavior

Completion, time, backtracking and requests for clarification.

04Preference with reason

Ask which version supports the decision and why—after comprehension.

Decision rule: advance only if comprehension improves without more critical errors or task friction. Report individual results and uncertainty; do not present a small synthetic study as market proof.
PRODUCT DECISION FRAMEWORKMeasurement Plan
BUSINESS HYPOTHESIS · NOT A FORECAST

Connect comprehension to conversion—without confusing correlation for proof.

If customers understand the complete financial impact before commitment, they may hesitate less at review and encounter fewer surprises after ordering. Each link needs its own evidence.

LEADING EVIDENCE

Comprehension

Participant accuracy for today, next bill, ongoing bill and trade-in conditions.

→
BEHAVIOR DIAGNOSTICS

Review friction

Backtracks, edit loops, exits and transitions from the flow to support.

→
PRIMARY OUTCOME

Review-to-submit

Confirmed orders divided by customers who reach Upgrade Impact review.

→
QUALITY GUARDRAILS

Retained success

Cancellations, returns, billing contacts and promotion disputes.

THE PRODUCT OWNER’S DECISION

Roll out only when the primary outcome improves and guardrails do not worsen.

Start with a participant study. If comprehension improves, run a controlled experiment with pre-defined duration, sample, segment checks and stopping rules. Investigate any conversion lift that arrives with worse support or cancellation outcomes.

Current evidence boundary: this project supplies a design hypothesis and measurement architecture. It contains no production analytics, verified retention lift or conversion forecast.
